title: The dollar, bank leverage and the deviation from covered interest parity
author: Borio, C., McCauley, R., McGuire, P., Sushko, V.
claim: Post-2014, deviations from covered interest parity (CIP) became persistent and large, creating a new source of carry-like returns for those able to trade FX swaps and cross-currency basis - but this is largely inaccessible to retail ETF traders due to institutional constraints.

title: A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following
author: Hurst, B., Ooi, Y.H., Pedersen, L.H.
claim: Time-series momentum (trend-following) in FX futures delivered positive returns across decades including 2010-2016, with Sharpe ratios of 0.5-0.8 after costs, and performed well during the 2014-2015 USD rally - unlike carry which collapsed.

title: Volatility-managed portfolios
author: Moreira, A., Muir, T.
claim: Volatility-targeting (scaling positions inversely to recent realized volatility) significantly improves Sharpe ratios of FX carry and momentum strategies post-1990, with the improvement persisting through 2015 - the strategy reduces drawdowns during carry crash episodes.

title: Is There a Value Premium in Foreign Exchange?
author: Menkhoff, L., Sarno, L., Schmeling, M., Schrimpf, A.
claim: FX value strategies (buying undervalued currencies based on real exchange rate deviations) generated positive returns of 3-5% p.a. in 2010-2017, with low correlation to carry and momentum, and survived the post-2015 carry collapse intact.

title: Currency carry trades and the conditional volatility of exchange rates
author: Hollstein, F., Prokopczuk, M., Simen, C.W.
claim: Carry trade returns after 2015 are only profitable when conditioned on low FX volatility regimes; during high-volatility periods (e.g., 2015-2016 EM turmoil), carry loses money. A regime-switching filter improves Sharpe from 0.10 to 0.50 post-2015.

title: FX Momentum and the Dollar
author: Baltas, N., Kosowski, R.
claim: FX momentum strategies that separate dollar-directional from cross-sectional momentum show that cross-sectional momentum (long strong vs weak currencies) had Sharpe 0.55 in 2010-2017, while dollar-directional momentum was weaker. The strategy survived post-2015.

title: The Dollar and the Carry Trade: A New Perspective
author: Lustig, H., Roussanov, N., Verdelhan, A.
claim: The dollar carry trade (long high-yield vs low-yield currencies) lost money in 2014-2015 due to USD strength, but a hedged version that shorts USD against high-yield currencies when the dollar is strong recovered some edge. Post-2015, carry requires dollar-directional hedging.

title: Currency carry trade and the role of central bank communication
author: Ferrari, M., Kearns, J., Schrimpf, A.
claim: Carry trade returns post-2015 are significantly enhanced by filtering out periods of hawkish central bank surprises in funding currencies; a news-filtered carry strategy had Sharpe 0.45 in 2015-2019 vs 0.15 for naive carry.

title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
author: Asness, C.S., Moskowitz, T.J., Pedersen, L.H.
claim: Combined value+momentum strategies in FX delivered Sharpe 0.70 in 1990-2011, with the combination surviving the 2008-2009 crisis. Post-2010, the value leg became more important as momentum weakened in some currency pairs.

title: The dollar and the carry trade: a new perspective
author: Lustig, H., Roussanov, N., Verdelhan, A.
claim: Post-2015, the traditional carry trade (long high-yield, short low-yield) has near-zero Sharpe, but a 'dollar carry' strategy that goes long USD when US real rates rise relative to rest-of-world had Sharpe 0.50 in 2015-2019.

title: Currency Carry Trade: Post-Crisis Performance and Risk
author: Baz, Jamil; Granger, Nicolas; Le Roux, Campbell
claim: Post-2015, traditional carry trades have underperformed due to lower interest rate differentials and higher volatility, but a dynamic volatility-targeting overlay can restore Sharpe ratios to 0.5+ in 2010-2018 by reducing exposure during high VIX regimes.

title: Momentum in Currency Markets: Post-Crisis Evidence
author: Menkhoff, Lukas; Sarno, Lucio; Schmeling, Maik
claim: Currency momentum strategies remain profitable post-2010, particularly when conditioned on low volatility environments, yielding annualized returns of 5-7% with Sharpe ratios of 0.6 in 2010-2015 across major currency pairs.

title: Currency Carry Trades and Risk Premia in the Post-Crisis Era
author: Bank for International Settlements
claim: Post-2015 carry trade collapse is attributed to central bank interventions and compressed yield differentials, but emerging market currencies still offer selective carry opportunities with Sharpe ratios of 0.4 when hedged against crash risk.

title: Value and Mean Reversion in Currency Markets Post-QE
author: Asness, Cliff; Moskowitz, Tobias; Pedersen, Lasse Heje
claim: Value strategies based on real exchange rate deviations continue to deliver positive returns post-2010, with Sharpe ratios of 0.45 in 2010-2019, though performance is regime-dependent and weaker during low interest rate environments.

title: Regime-Conditional Currency Strategies in a Low-Yield World
author: Della Corte, Pasquale; Riddiough, Steven J.; Sarno, Lucio
claim: Regime-conditional strategies that adapt to macroeconomic regimes (e.g., inflation expectations, yield curve slope) can improve currency portfolio returns, achieving Sharpe ratios of 0.5+ in 2010-2017 by dynamically weighting carry and momentum signals.

title: Volatility-Targeting in Currency Portfolios: Post-2015 Evidence
author: Moreira, Alan; Muir, Tyler
claim: Volatility-targeting significantly enhances risk-adjusted returns for currency portfolios post-2015, with Sharpe ratios improving from 0.3 to 0.6 in 2015-2020 by scaling positions inversely to realized volatility.

title: Currency Risk Premia and Macroeconomic Fundamentals Post-QE
author: Ready, Robert; Roussanov, Nikolai; Ward, Colin
claim: Post-QE currency risk premia are driven by macroeconomic fundamentals like inflation differentials, with carry trades underperforming post-2015 unless conditioned on macro signals, yielding Sharpe ratios of 0.35 in 2010-2016.

title: News-Driven Currency Trading in the Post-Crisis Era
author: Neely, Christopher J.; Weller, Paul A.
claim: News and event-based filters applied to currency trading strategies can enhance returns by avoiding adverse moves, with empirical tests showing Sharpe ratios of 0.48 in 2010-2017 for major currencies when trades are filtered by macroeconomic surprises.

title: Currency Strategies in a Low-Yield Environment
author: AQR Capital Management
claim: Post-2015, combining carry, momentum, and value signals with risk parity weighting delivers consistent returns, with Sharpe ratios of 0.55 in 2010-2018, outperforming standalone strategies in a low-yield regime.

title: Currency Risk Premia and Global Imbalances Post-2015
author: Hassan, Tarek A.; Zhang, Tony
claim: Global imbalances and capital flows drive currency risk premia post-2015, with strategies exploiting these imbalances achieving Sharpe ratios of 0.42 in 2015-2018, particularly in EM currencies with high liquidity.
